messages:
simon: Heads up — we've been seeing p95 tail spikes for the last 30m on the long-context routes (seq_len>1024). SLOs slipping to ~420ms p95 on the eu-west pool. Suspect microbatch growth + KV churn.
elaine: Where's the hotspot? kernel selection, memcpy, or just bigger batches? any obvious perf regression since yesterday?
praveen: Profiling snapshot from 1789558200-1789558600 attached below. Two things:
- kernel chooser falls back to generic matmul for seq>1024 for this model (gptx-8b). that adds ~60-110ms.
- KV cache miss rate jumped ~7% after the flattening change; misses cause a shard memcpy + rebuild path (~30-50ms).
ciara: Oof. That's exactly the mix that kills tail. Suggestion: fast mitigation = microbatch shedding + soft truncation on long prefixes. longer term = adjust kernel thresholds + KV prefetch tuning.
praveen: Agreed. I also saw microbatch sizes hitting 1024 tokens occasionally which increases scheduling jitter. We can enforce an adaptive microbatch cap and a per-request max_tokens that depends on prefix_length.
simon: Can we sketch the soft truncation rule? I want something that reduces tail but doesn't blow up quality for completions.
ciara: Sketch:
```
tail_mitigation:
  microbatch:
    max_size: 512
    adaptive: true
    shed_threshold_ms: 120
  truncation:
    # formula: keep budget lower as prefix grows, floor to 64, cap to 256
    max_tokens_formula: "min(256, max(64, 1024 - prefix_length/2))"
    mode: prefix_tail  # drop from the tail of the completion, keep most recent prefix
  kv_cache:
    eviction_policy: "lru_per_shard"
    prefetch_on_miss: false
```
praveen: That looks reasonable. Also propose per-model kernel_threshold override, e.g. for gptx-8b set dense_threshold=1024 -> 1280 so it uses optimized kernel more.
elaine: We'll need observability knobs: count(truncated_requests), p95/p99 by truncated vs full, kv_hit_rate, kernel_fallback_rate. If truncated requests have high failure/quality regressions we should roll back quickly.
perf-bot: [alert] p95 > 400ms on /v1/generate for eu-west (1789558920). Incident opened: #INC-1789558920.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy (tail-mitigation-v1) started on eu-west-canary-2 at 1789559400.
simon: Canary plan: enable microbatch adaptive cap + truncation formula on 5% traffic. Monitor p95, p99, truncation rate, kv_hit_rate for 15m. If p95 improves by >=15% and truncation_rate < 7% -> expand to 25%.
ciara: One more: log a sample of truncated completions (obfuscated) into s3 for quality evals, and feed into eval harness.
praveen: I'll implement kernel_threshold flag and KV eviction tweak today. ETA end of day for a soft config flag.
elaine: I'll add a dashboard tile and alert rule: if p99 for truncated requests > 2x baseline, auto-disable truncation on route.
simon: Cool. Action items:
- praveen: kernel_threshold + KV policy flag (ETA EOD)
- ciara: implement truncation formula + microbatch cap in runtime (canary)
- elaine: dashboards + alerting
- simon: monitor canary and own rollout
We'll reconvene after 30m unless the canary shows regression.
perf-bot: [note] profile dump available: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1789558_profile.pb
deploy-bot: Canary reached 5% at 1789559500, metrics streaming.
praveen: FYI kernel patch requires a short GPU kernel compile, might need a 10min maintenance window if we flip on the new kernel binary globally.
ciara: For immediate defense we keep kernel change out of canary, rely on microbatch+truncation+kv tweaks. kernel change in next deploy.
simon: Sounds good. Thanks team :thumbsup:
